hypotheses.mechanism: An excessively high or poorly tuned learning rate causes gradient updates to oscillate around the loss minimum, preventing stable convergence. This manifests as latent_mse@4 rising above latent_mse@3 and limiting representation alignment gains. Reducing the learning rate will dampen update variance, enabling smoother descent toward lower reconstruction error and higher cosine similarity.
hypotheses.statement: The non-monotonic latent_mse trajectory and plateauing cosine similarity indicate optimization_instability caused by an ill-scaled learning rate.
hypotheses.title: Optimization Instability from Suboptimal Learning Rate
